title: Intervals: sort by end
summary: Fewest intervals to remove so the rest don't overlap; touching ends are fine. Sort by end and keep each interval that starts at or after the last kept end. O(n log n).
code: # Keep the interval that ends first; it leaves the most room for the rest.
for start, end in sorted(intervals, key=lambda interval: interval[1]):
triggers: the most non-overlapping intervals, or the fewest removals to get there
schedule as many activities as possible on one shared resource
prompts: A single meeting room has many booking requests, some overlapping. Accept as many as possible; how many must be turned down?
A festival stage receives set requests with start and end times. Back-to-back sets are fine, overlaps are not. Keep the largest number of sets.
invariant: The kept intervals don't overlap, and no compatible choice of the same number of intervals ends earlier than last_end.
mantra: Sort by end; keep what fits after the last kept end.
pitfalls: Sort by end, not start: an early-starting long interval can block many short ones.
Half-open intervals may touch, so keep when start >= last_end.
Count the kept intervals and subtract; removing while scanning is error-prone.

anchors.name: Minimum Number of Arrows to Burst Balloons
anchors.trick: Same greedy on closed intervals: a new arrow only when start > last_end.

anchors.name: Maximum Length of Pair Chain
anchors.trick: Count the kept pairs; a chain needs start > last_end.

anchors.name: Merge Intervals
anchors.trick: Different rule: sort by start and extend the last end.

mutations.explanation: Sorting by start keeps an early, long interval that blocks shorter ones: [[1, 10], [2, 3], [4, 5]] removes 2 instead of 1.
Treats touching intervals as overlapping: [[1, 2], [2, 3]] removes 1 instead of 0.
